NKJV.1: Then Zophar the Naamathite answered and said:
NKJV.2: “Should not the multitude of words be answered? And should a man full of talk be vindicated?
NKJV.3: Should your empty talk make men hold their peace? And when you mock, should no one rebuke you?
NKJV.4: For you have said, ‘My doctrine is pure, And I am clean in your eyes.’
NKJV.5: But oh, that God would speak, And open His lips against you,
NKJV.6: That He would show you the secrets of wisdom! For they would double your prudence. Know therefore that God exacts from you Less than your iniquity deserves.
NKJV.7: “Can  you search out the deep things of God? Can you find out the limits of the Almighty?
NKJV.8: They are higher than heaven— what can you do? Deeper than Sheol— what can you know?
NKJV.9: Their measure is longer than the earth And broader than the sea.
NKJV.10: “If He passes by, imprisons, and gathers to judgment, Then who can hinder Him?
NKJV.11: For He knows deceitful men; He sees wickedness also. Will He not then consider it?
NKJV.12: For an empty-headed man will be wise, When a wild donkey’s colt is born a man.
NKJV.13: “If you would prepare your heart, And stretch out your hands toward Him;
NKJV.14: If iniquity were in your hand, and you put it far away, And would not let wickedness dwell in your tents;
NKJV.15: Then surely you could lift up your face without spot; Yes, you could be steadfast, and not fear;
NKJV.16: Because you would forget your misery, And remember it as waters that have passed away,
NKJV.17: And your life would be brighter than noonday. Though you were dark, you would be like the morning.
NKJV.18: And you would be secure, because there is hope; Yes, you would dig around you, and take your rest in safety.
NKJV.19: You would also lie down, and no one would make you afraid; Yes, many would court your favor.
NKJV.20: But the eyes of the wicked will fail, And they shall not escape, And their hope—loss of life!”

ESV.1: Then Zophar the Naamathite answered and said:
ESV.2: “Should a multitude of words go unanswered, and a man full of talk be judged right?
ESV.3: Should your babble silence men, and when you mock, shall no one shame you?
ESV.4: For you say, ‘My doctrine is pure, and I am clean in God's  eyes.’
ESV.5: But oh, that God would speak and open his lips to you,
ESV.6: and that he would tell you the secrets of wisdom! For he is manifold in understanding.  Know then that God exacts of you less than your guilt deserves.
ESV.7: “Can you find out the deep things of God? Can you find out the limit of the Almighty?
ESV.8: It is higher than heaven  — what can you do? Deeper than Sheol — what can you know?
ESV.9: Its measure is longer than the earth and broader than the sea.
ESV.10: If he passes through and imprisons and summons the court, who can turn him back?
ESV.11: For he knows worthless men; when he sees iniquity, will he not consider it?
ESV.12: But a stupid man will get understanding when a wild donkey's colt is born a man!
ESV.13: “If you prepare your heart, you will stretch out your hands toward him.
ESV.14: If iniquity is in your hand, put it far away, and let not injustice dwell in your tents.
ESV.15: Surely then you will lift up your face without blemish; you will be secure and will not fear.
ESV.16: You will forget your misery; you will remember it as waters that have passed away.
ESV.17: And your life will be brighter than the noonday; its darkness will be like the morning.
ESV.18: And you will feel secure, because there is hope; you will look around and take your rest in security.
ESV.19: You will lie down, and none will make you afraid; many will court your favor.
ESV.20: But the eyes of the wicked will fail; all way of escape will be lost to them, and their hope is to breathe their last.”

NLT.1: Then Zophar the Naamathite replied to Job:
NLT.2:
“Shouldn’t someone answer this torrent of words?
Is a person proved innocent just by a lot of talking?
NLT.3:
Should I remain silent while you babble on?
When you mock God, shouldn’t someone make you ashamed?
NLT.4:
You claim, ‘My beliefs are pure,’
and ‘I am clean in the sight of God.’
NLT.5:
If only God would speak;
if only he would tell you what he thinks!
NLT.6:
If only he would tell you the secrets of wisdom,
for true wisdom is not a simple matter.
Listen! God is doubtless punishing you
far less than you deserve!
NLT.7:
“Can you solve the mysteries of God?
Can you discover everything about the Almighty?
NLT.8:
Such knowledge is higher than the heavens —
and who are you?
It is deeper than the underworld —
what do you know?
NLT.9:
It is broader than the earth
and wider than the sea.
NLT.10:
If God comes and puts a person in prison
or calls the court to order, who can stop him?
NLT.11:
For he knows those who are false,
and he takes note of all their sins.
NLT.12:
An empty-headed person won’t become wise
any more than a wild donkey can bear a human child.
NLT.13:
“If only you would prepare your heart
and lift up your hands to him in prayer!
NLT.14:
Get rid of your sins,
and leave all iniquity behind you.
NLT.15:
Then your face will brighten with innocence.
You will be strong and free of fear.
NLT.16:
You will forget your misery;
it will be like water flowing away.
NLT.17:
Your life will be brighter than the noonday.
Even darkness will be as bright as morning.
NLT.18:
Having hope will give you courage.
You will be protected and will rest in safety.
NLT.19:
You will lie down unafraid,
and many will look to you for help.
NLT.20:
But the wicked will be blinded.
They will have no escape.
Their only hope is death.”

AMP.1: Then Zophar the Naamathite answered and said,
AMP.2:
"Shall a multitude of words not be answered?
And should a talkative man [making such a long-winded defense] be acquitted?
AMP.3:
"Should your boasts and babble silence men?
And shall you scoff and no one put you to shame?
AMP.4:
"For you have said, 'My teaching (doctrine) [that God knowingly afflicts the righteous] is pure,
And I am innocent in your eyes.'
AMP.5:
"But oh, that God would speak,
And open His lips [to speak] against you,
AMP.6:
And [that He would] show you the secrets of wisdom!
For sound wisdom has two sides.
Know therefore that God forgets a part of your wickedness and guilt.
AMP.7:
"Can you discover the depths of God?
Can you [by searching] discover the limits of the Almighty [ascend to His heights, extend to His widths, and comprehend His infinite perfection]?
AMP.8:
"His wisdom is as high as the heights of heaven. What can you do?
It is deeper than Sheol (the nether world, the place of the dead). What can you know?
AMP.9:
"It is longer in measure [and scope] than the earth,
And broader than the sea.
AMP.10:
"If God passes by or arrests,
Or calls an assembly [of judgment], who can restrain Him?
[If He is against a man, who can call Him to account for it?]
AMP.11:
"For He recognizes and knows false and worthless men,
And He sees wickedness, will He not consider it?
AMP.12:
"But a hollow (empty-headed) man will become intelligent and wise
[Only] when the colt of a wild donkey is born as a man.
AMP.13:
"If you direct your heart [on the right path]
And stretch out your hands to Him,
AMP.14:
If sin is in your hand, put it far away [from you],
And do not let wrongdoing dwell in your tents;
AMP.15:
Then, indeed, you could lift up your face [to Him] without moral defect,
And you would be firmly established and secure and not fear.
AMP.16:
"For you would forget your trouble;
You would remember it as waters that have passed by.
AMP.17:
"And your life would be brighter than the noonday;
Darkness [then] would be like the morning.
AMP.18:
"Then you would trust [with confidence], because there is hope;
You would look around you and rest securely.
AMP.19:
"You would lie down with no one to frighten you,
And many would entreat and seek your favor.
AMP.20:
"But the eyes of the wicked will fail,
And they will not escape [the justice of God];
And their hope is to breathe their last [and die]."

NET.1: Then Zophar the Naamathite spoke up and said:
NET.2: “Should not this abundance of words be answered, or should this talkative man be vindicated?
NET.3: Will your idle talk reduce people to silence, and will no one rebuke you when you mock?
NET.4: For you have said, ‘My teaching is flawless, and I am pure in your sight.’
NET.5: But if only God would speak, if only he would open his lips against you,
NET.6: and reveal to you the secrets of wisdom — for true wisdom has two sides — so that you would know that God has forgiven some of your sins.
NET.7: “Can you discover the essence of God? Can you find out the perfection of the Almighty?
NET.8: It is higher than the heavens — what can you do? It is deeper than Sheol — what can you know?
NET.9: Its measure is longer than the earth, and broader than the sea.
NET.10: If he comes by and confines you and convenes a court, then who can prevent him?
NET.11: For he knows deceitful men; when he sees evil, will he not consider it?
NET.12: But an empty man will become wise, when a wild donkey’s colt is born a human being.
NET.13: “As for you, if you prove faithful, and if you stretch out your hands toward him,
NET.14: if iniquity is in your hand — put it far away, and do not let evil reside in your tents.
NET.15: For then you will lift up your face without blemish; you will be securely established and will not fear.
NET.16: For you will forget your trouble; you will remember it like water that has flowed away.
NET.17: And life will be brighter than the noonday; though there be darkness, it will be like the morning.
NET.18: And you will be secure, because there is hope; you will be protected and will take your rest in safety.
NET.19: You will lie down with no one to make you afraid, and many will seek your favor.
NET.20: But the eyes of the wicked fail, and escape eludes them; their one hope is to breathe their last.”

MSG.1: Now it was the turn of Zophar from Naamath:
MSG.2:
"What a flood of words! Shouldn't we put a stop to it?
Should this kind of loose talk be permitted?
MSG.3:
Job, do you think you can carry on like this and we'll say nothing?
That we'll let you rail and mock and not step in?
MSG.4:
You claim, 'My doctrine is sound
and my conduct impeccable.'
MSG.5:
How I wish God would give you a piece of his mind,
tell you what's what!
MSG.6:
I wish he'd show you how wisdom looks from the inside,
for true wisdom is mostly 'inside.'
But you can be sure of this,
you haven't gotten half of what you deserve.
MSG.7:
"Do you think you can explain the mystery of God?
Do you think you can diagram God Almighty?
MSG.8:
God is far higher than you can imagine,
far deeper than you can comprehend,
MSG.9:
Stretching farther than earth's horizons,
far wider than the endless ocean.
MSG.10:
If he happens along, throws you in jail
then hauls you into court, can you do anything about it?
MSG.11:
He sees through vain pretensions,
spots evil a long way off—
no one pulls the wool over his eyes!
MSG.12:
Hollow men, hollow women, will wise up
about the same time mules learn to talk.
MSG.13:
"Still, if you set your heart on God
and reach out to him,
MSG.14:
If you scrub your hands of sin
and refuse to entertain evil in your home,
MSG.15:
You'll be able to face the world unashamed
and keep a firm grip on life, guiltless and fearless.
MSG.16:
You'll forget your troubles;
they'll be like old, faded photographs.
MSG.17:
Your world will be washed in sunshine,
every shadow dispersed by dayspring.
MSG.18:
Full of hope, you'll relax, confident again;
you'll look around, sit back, and take it easy.
MSG.19:
Expansive, without a care in the world,
you'll be hunted out by many for your blessing.
MSG.20:
But the wicked will see none of this.
They're headed down a dead-end road
with nothing to look forward to—nothing."
